request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: (patient's name)
Age: 84 years old
Gender: Female
Admission Date: (date of admission)
Discharge Date: (date of discharge)
Length of Stay: (number of days of hospital stay)
Clinical Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted due to her underlying medical conditions including type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She also had a history of amblyopia OD and a resolved branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) in the left eye. During her hospital stay, she was treated with Eyefolate™ capsules and no further complications were reported during the course of treatment.

Clinical Progress:
In October 2013, the patient's best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/150 OD and 20/25 OS. The OS fundus photo showed a large macular aneurysm (MA) in the superior temporal region with exudates. After being prescribed the Eyefolate™ capsules, the BCVA of the left eye improved to 20/20 in August 2014. Further improvement was seen in December 2014 when the large exudates almost completely resolved in OS (Fig. b). In January 2016, the BCVA was 20/400 OD and 20/25 OS, and the MA was resolved as shown in the OS fundus photo (Fig. c) during 2016.

Follow-up:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition with instructions to continue taking prescribed medications and regular follow-up appointments with her primary care physician to monitor her diabetes and hypertension. A referral to an ophthalmologist was also recommended to monitor her vision and perpetuate the effectiveness of the treatment.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The summary does not name a clear principal diagnosis, because the clinical diagnosis section is withheld. The narrative says the patient was admitted because of underlying conditions (type 2 diabetes and hypertension), but the treatment and the clinical progress both concern the eye. The condition treated was a retinal macroaneurysm with exudates in the left eye, treated with Eyefolate (a folate preparation).

A retinal macroaneurysm is coded to H35.0 (background retinopathy and retinal vascular changes), which includes retinal macroaneurysm in ICD-10. It would be H35 at the three-character level.

The alternative is diabetic retinopathy, E11.3 with H36.0*. That would require the clinician to document it as diabetic, and the record does not. The condition is described as a macular aneurysm after BRVO, so I will not assume a diabetic link.

The admission statement points to diabetes, but the treatment and course concern the retinal condition. This is the condition investigated and treated, so I will code it as principal.

CODE: H35
